title: CS amp, diode-connected load
description: Common-source stage with a diode-connected transistor as the load. The load's low-impedance $\approx 1/g_m$ sets a gain that is a ratio of transconductances, $A_v = g_{m,in}/(g_{m,load} + g_{ds,in} + g_{ds,load})$, which is well-controlled across process and temperature - the classic teaching load. The load is a composed child (pick its device table to the opposite polarity). Because it is diode-connected, its drain-source voltage equals its own gate-source voltage, so the bind declares the connection and the table is read along that diagonal - there is no drop to estimate, and no polarity knob to set, since the diagonal follows whichever sign convention the table itself uses. The output DC level sits one load $V_{GS}$ below the supply.

params.note: a diode load gives a modest, well-controlled gain

params.name: gbw_margin

params.name: gm_id

params.name: gm_id_load
params.note: load inversion: lower gm/ID gives a higher gain (smaller load gm) but costs the output more headroom and adds noise

doc.title: Diode-connected load device
doc.description: One device diode-connected (gate tied to drain), so its vds equals its vgs. Carries the stage current, exposing its transconductance (which sets the gain and the output level), its output conductance, and its gate-source drop.

rows.name: V_out
rows.note: output DC level: one diode drop below the supply

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: the resistance this stage presents at its output: the diode load's own transconductance dominates it — both output conductances add in parallel and move it by under a tenth. The gain assumes a capacitive load, so nothing here models a resistive one; this row is what a composing parent checks its own loading against

rows.name: Av
rows.note: input gm into the diode load conductance (~load gm) plus both output conductances

rows.name: GBW
rows.note: the gm/ID currency, and a good estimate of the unity-gain frequency only while Av0 is comfortably above 1. A diode load is exactly the regime where it is not: a single-pole stage crosses unity at f_p*sqrt(Av0^2 - 1), so at Av0 near 1.4-1.5 the literal crossing sits 25-30% below this row. Read it as transconductance per load capacitance, not as a measured bandwidth

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: the diode load's own drain noise (vnth_m_load*gm_load) referred to the input by 1/gm_in

rows.name: cgg_in
rows.note: estimate: the capacitance the input terminal presents — this stage's gate capacitance and nothing else. Gate capacitance only, because the Miller term needs the gate-drain fraction and these tables do not carry it, so a driving stage sees more than this. No rule reads it

rows.name: I_q
rows.note: estimate: quiescent supply current — the branch current, which here is an OUTPUT of the sizing rather than a setting: the bandwidth spec fixes gm, and the chosen inversion divides it down to a current. The datasheet line for comparing designs; no rule reads it

rules.note: gm/ID cannot exceed the weak-inversion ceiling of the data
